speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) for each year in the past three years, what has been the year-on-year increase in average rental per square foot for HDB commercial units (i) rented directly from HDB (ii) sublet from a master tenant that rents from HDB and (iii) sublet from a private owner, respectively; and (b) whether HDB is considering approaches to keep rental rates in check in each of these categories.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Housing and Development Board (HDB) plans its towns and estates comprehensively to ensure that residents have convenient access to affordable goods and services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A key measure is to ensure a good supply of shops in every HDB estate and town, so that there is healthy competition.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Of these, about 8,500 are sold and hence, privately owned, and about 7,000 are rented out by HDB.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For shops rented out by HDB, there are various measures in place to keep rents stable.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: All shops are typically rented out by HDB for a period of three years.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When the existing tenancy is due for renewal, the rent for the next tenancy period is assessed by professional valuers appointed by HDB, taking into account recent rents of comparable premises in the vicinity as well as prevailing market and local conditions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Over the last three years, average rents increased at a moderate pace of between 1.3% and 3.3% per year.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For all new generation neighbourhood centres, new eating houses and new supermarkets, HDB applies the price quality method (PQM) tender with 60% of points assigned to the quality of the operator, which includes aspects such as good track record and community initiatives.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Such tenders allow HDB to holistically evaluate both price and quality factors instead of simply awarding to the highest priced bid.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As for HDB shops that are sold, their rents are determined by their respective owners, similar to any other private property.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We are aware that per-square-foot rents for privately-owned HDB shops have seen a steep increase recently.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This coincided with a higher proportion of rental transactions involving smaller sized units, which tend to command higher per-square-foot rents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB ceased the sale of HDB shops in 1998 and now rents out shops to businesses directly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are around 740 privately-owned HDB shops sold on 30-year leases, more than 80% of which have less than 10 years of lease remaining.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These shops will progressively be returned to HDB and then tenanted out.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The remaining of around 7,700 privately-held HDB shops were sold on 99-year leases and they still have more than 30 years on their lease remaining.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB will continue to provide new shops in new public housing developments and we will also inject new retail supply to meet demand in existing estates when necessary, including the option of selectively acquiring privately-held HDB shops if needed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Overall, we will see an increase in the supply of HDB shops, a higher proportion of which will be directly rented out by the HDB.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the rents for HDB shops tended out for medical facilities, I will provide the average rent per square foot.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is because shop units of different sizes and the absolute rent quantum, therefore, does not provide a meaningful comparison.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For vacated units in existing HDB blocks, which are typically in older estates, the average rent per square foot increased from $5.70 in 2020, to $11.40 in the first half of 2025.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In comparison, the average rent per square foot is higher for new lettings in new Build-To-Order (BTO) developments, which increased from $12.30 in 2020, to $39.30 in the first half of 2025.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The difference is mainly due to the fact that these new leases are located in newer residential areas where the shop units are newer and the businesses may consider them to be more attractive.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Until recently, we have been letting out most shop units for general practitioner (GP) clinics purely based on price.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To improve quality outcomes and to lower the bidding pressure, HDB and the Ministry of Health (MOH) have started piloting PQM tenders for GP clinics since May this year, with 70% of points assigned to the quality of the operator.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On sublet rents, HDB currently does not collect these data, which are part of the contractual agreements between HDB tenants and their sub-tenants.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We understand the concerns that sublet rents could increase more significantly than what HDB charges the main tenant.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will continue to monitor the situation and explore appropriate ways to provide more information to all stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The first is on the rental increases by category.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I think the Senior Minister of State talked about the increase for private-owned properties as well as properties rented directly by HDB.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But I did ask about that category of a sublet rents.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I understand that that has gone up significantly, and if HDB's increases are only in the 1.3% to 3.5% range to the master tenant, I do believe that is going up much more for their sublets.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And in particular, do the opening hours of the clinics qualify as markers of quality?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I ask this because I have asked this a few times in the House.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In my area in Woodlands North Plaza, which is a big commercial centre, we have three medical clinics, none of which operate after 5.00 pm, and only till 12.00 pm on Saturdays, which is really unhelpful, especially for young families and families with seniors, where people have to take leave just to take their loved ones to the clinic.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I have shared that HDB and MOH have started piloting the PQM tender for GP clinics.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For the quality condition, where 70% of the points are awarded in this category, the following areas are considered.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: One is the care model, whether the clinic is offering multi-disciplinary care.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The second area is the manpower quality, whether or not the assistants in the clinic have undergone training, whether the staff have undergone training.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And thirdly, specifically on the operation side of the house, which is the operating hours.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I hope that answers the Member's second question.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Moving forward, I have shared that for new neighbourhood centres, we are applying the PQM model.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And apart from looking at the generic affordability within the quality condition, we might look at how there can be a better provisioning of information with regards to sublet rent as part of the quality metrics.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I have a supplementary question on the rental in the resale shops, shops that are sold by HDB.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I welcome the openness of MND to consider all options, including compulsory acquisitions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But that said, I do want to also take a step back and make sure that we remember the larger picture, which is that the sold shops are privately owned.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And the owners of these shops have obviously made their business calculations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And if I may refer Members to a recent Straits Times commentary by Prof Sing Tien Foo, who is a professor in the Department of Real Estate at the National University of Singapore, he did share that, ultimately, there is a limit as to how much private landlords can raise rents before losing their tenants.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think that we have to allow market forces to play out.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I just wanted to understand for subsequent renewals of the GP clinics at HDB estates, would there also be a similar requirement to have the quality of healthcare provision, being assessed as part of the renewal condition?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And secondly, in terms of the PQM method for new tenders across other trade mix, such as dental and so on, are these also being considered?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I am sorry, I did not quite catch the second question, but I will respond to the first one first.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I mentioned, HDB and MOH embarked on our first PQM tender in May this year.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This was awarded in August, so we are still looking at the experience of conducting these PQM tenders, and we are thinking what would be the appropriate steady-state model.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But indeed, because medical services are essential to the community, I would say that it is more likely that we would be implementing PQM to more clinics rather than less.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And for sure, new GP clinics in HDB estates will use the PQM approach.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: Extending the PQM method to other trade mix like dental and all that.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Yes, I had mentioned in my main reply that for all new neighbourhood centres, we are applying PQM for our HDB rental shops.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I ask this because I understand that some of the owners of the current HDB-sold flats often lease them out to the highest possible rent and frequently, this could result in units being leased to businesses, like spas or licensed moneylenders who can pay a higher rent.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: This, in turn, can lead to an undesirable business mix in the neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Thus, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether HDB would consider accelerating the acquisition of HDB-sold flats, in particular in the Nanyang division, where we have new BTO flats, but we do not have new supply of HDB shops and there is a shortage of eating houses.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I will come back to the Member as to whether or not we have selectively acquired any HDB-sold shops before.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I do not think we have done so, but let me come back to you on that point, because I have mentioned that this is not our current policy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And if we should look into it, it would be based on what I have shared with the Member Mr Henry Kwek earlier, who had asked a similar question, we would have to look at the overall supply of shops in the area.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have to decide whether or not these are essential services that we are concerned about.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have to determine if the market forces at play are not at the right balance, where residents are being adequately cared for.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And it is only where all these conditions are met that we will consider selectively acquiring shops.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I will just like to share where the difficulty level is.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: You must understand that for the specific situations that Members are most concerned about, those sold shops were probably sold at a high market price, in the first place, to begin with.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, what Members seem to be suggesting is to ask HDB to acquire that already highly priced sold shop.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Another possibility is to selectively acquire shops around it to increase supply.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But if we are looking at selectively acquiring shops around that sold shop, which is charging a very high rental, leading to high product prices and so on and so forth, that is something that we can consider, but we will have to look at the overall supply of shops in the market, and what are the products and services they are offering.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My question pertains to her point in her main answer.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I believe Senior Minister of State repeated it in her reply to Member Ms Mariam Jaafar.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Senior Minister of State said that HDB will continue to monitor this area.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, rather than just monitor it, perhaps HDB should take a further step forward in line with what she said about IRAS data, for example, and compile it for the general public.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, I have mentioned that we are monitoring the situation and by that I mean that we will have to look at the data that is available.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Some of the data might not be very clean, in particular, because some of the disclosure of the data is disclosed to IRAS, and then the Urban Redevelopment Authority pulls the data from IRAS, and then, we post it on Real Estate Information System (REALIS), which is URA-maintained.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we do have data that we can look at.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, while we maintain an open stance that the HDB, while promoting greater transparency of data and we can potentially act, I would just like to caveat that we may not also want to overstep, because there are market forces at play.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have to let business owners, whether or not it is the landlord or the sublet tenant, make their decisions based on what they deem is relevant and suitable for their business considerations.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In spite of my best endeavours, we only cleared 14 PQs today.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
